component_records.title: Bid governance, compliance and contract obligations
component_records.description: A single compliance register tracks every legal, contractual and pricing obligation the RFP imposes and shows where the proposal satisfies it: acceptance of the City's terms and conditions, ownership of all data, materials and documentation in the City, no blanket proprietary designation and advance notice of any confidential material, insurance certification and underwriter's endorsement with an admitted Washington surety before work starts, and the proposer bearing its own bid costs. The register also records the City's sole authority over public-disclosure treatment and the risk of rejection for referencing non-City terms. It is maintained by the engagement director and reviewed at each phase gate.

component_records.title: Selection-stage commitment: demos, due diligence and negotiations
component_records.description: The named bid team commits to the City's selection calendar as a firm obligation, not an option. The same engagement director, solution architect and module leads who will run the implementation are the people who present the functional and technical demo in December 2024, attend the January 2025 due diligence review with financial statements, reference contacts and security documentation ready, and enter contract negotiations from January 2025 with a mandate to sign. Availability is confirmed in the proposal with named individuals and a single point of contact, and the team holds the December and January windows free of conflicting engagements so a City reschedule can be absorbed.

component_records.title: Requirements response and clarification programme
component_records.description: The team completes the City's separate Requirements document in its original Word format, rating every line item on the City's five-point scale (4, 3, 2, 0, F) with a comment of no more than 100 words explaining how the function is met, naming the third-party product for any rating of 3, giving the estimated cost for any rating of 2, and giving the release month and year for any rating of F. No hyperlinks, no cross-references to other line items, no format or page-break changes, and no 'standard functionality' answers. The same discipline drives the demo: the team prepares against the City's Demo Script, staffs the December 2024 demo and January 2025 due diligence, and stands ready for follow-up demonstrations and clarification. Written questions are lodged by the August 28, 2024 deadline and all addenda are incorporated.

component_records.title: Solution architecture and integration design
component_records.description: A documented architecture for the integrated ERP covering the Financial modules (General Ledger, Budget, Project and Grant Accounting, Purchasing and Contract Management, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Capital Assets, Enterprise Cashiering) and the HCM modules (Human Resources, Time and Attendance, Payroll), with a single audit trail across all modules capturing user, date, time stamp and before/after values. Integration is designed and built for the interfaces the City needs, including any best-of-breed HCM component, using published APIs and a named integration toolset with a documented methodology. The design is validated against the City's Requirements document during fit-gap so that gaps are known before configuration starts.

component_records.title: Phased implementation programme and project management
component_records.description: A phased plan, recommended by the bidder and submitted for City approval, running from March 2025 to Go Live for all modules in scope by January 1, 2027. The plan sets out phases, tasks, milestones, dependencies and approval gates, names City resources by role, responsibility and average hours per month, and names vendor resources on the same basis. A process improvement strategy runs alongside configuration so the City captures the best practices it is buying, and a business change management methodology with defined tools is applied from mobilization onward. Progress is reported monthly against the plan and the Go Live date.

component_records.title: Data conversion by module
component_records.description: A data conversion methodology plus a module-by-module conversion plan stating, for each module, the years of history and the data elements to be converted, the extraction and validation approach, and the reconciliation and sign-off the City performs before load. Conversion is rehearsed at least twice into a test environment before the final cutover load, with exception reports returned to the City for correction. The plan covers Financial and HCM data, including payroll history and balances needed for W2 and leave processing.

component_records.title: Configuration, report development and testing
component_records.description: Configuration of every module in scope to the City's requirements, with any modification identified in the Requirements document carrying an estimated cost so the City can decide whether to accept it. Report development delivers the City's operational and statutory reports on a documented approach, with a report inventory agreed during fit-gap and built and validated in the test environment. Testing follows a written methodology and toolset covering unit, integration, conversion, security and user acceptance testing, with City sign-off required at each stage and defects tracked to closure before cutover.

component_records.title: Training and change management
component_records.description: Role-based training for the City's named users, delivered through a documented training methodology and toolset: train-the-trainer for internal champions, hands-on sessions per module, quick-reference materials and a sandbox environment for practice before Go Live. Training is sequenced with the phased rollout so each group is trained close to its cutover, and attendance and competency are tracked. Change management activities — stakeholder mapping, communications, readiness assessments and adoption measurement — run from mobilization through post-go-live stabilization.

component_records.title: Hosted platform, security and disaster recovery
component_records.description: The production ERP is hosted in the bidder's data centres with stated locations and redundancy, with an on-premises option available and priced separately. The service includes scheduled software updates with a published timeline, remote access over supported technologies, mobile hardware and OS support, and a backup strategy with defined retention and restore testing. Security covers the security model and standards met, SSO and SAML administration, multi-factor authentication, and a written breach process stating how the City is notified, the response the bidder provides and who bears the cost. Disaster recovery is described at baseline and premium levels so the City can choose.

component_records.title: Post go-live support and service levels
component_records.description: Support begins at Go Live and runs for the contract term: stated support hours, guaranteed response times by severity, named resources, and a documented escalation path with City-facing contacts. Baseline and premium support levels are compared side by side so the City can price the difference, and user groups and conferences available to City staff are listed. Post go-live tools and services include a stabilization period with on-site or remote hypercare, a health-check review at 30 and 90 days, and a continuous improvement backlog carried into the maintenance years.

component_records.title: Pricing on the Exhibit A template
component_records.description: Pricing is submitted on the City's Exhibit A template as Section 3 of the response, with a separate sheet for each deployment option (SaaS and on-premises). It quotes the Financials deployment at 130 named and 85 concurrent users and the HCM deployment at 400 FTEs and 744 W2s, prices each named Financial and HCM module line, prices Year 1 software and all implementation services (implementation, data conversion, training, report development, integration, travel and other), and prices subscription/maintenance for each of Years 2 through 10. Every block carries stated assumptions, the Sub-Total and Total lines are completed, all taxes and available discounts are included, and the pricing is held valid for 180 days from the response date.

items.text: Requirements document not in hand, so scope and price rest on an unseen file. The functional scope is defined by a separate Requirements document issued with the RFP, and the current-systems tables in Section 3 are not reproduced. The bid team must rate and price every line item in a document it has not seen, so the implementation estimate and the Exhibit A totals could be built on a scope that turns out larger or different. If the document arrives late or is materially bigger than assumed, the bid is either underpriced or has to be reworked close to the September 17, 2024 deadline. The RFP makes the Requirements document the definition of scope and the basis of the Section 2 response, yet it is a separate file the bidder must obtain; the solution's own assumption that every line item is answered and priced depends entirely on it.
items.reason: Cited sources show scope defined in a separate Requirements document, rating required per item, September 17 deadline, Exhibit A pricing.

items.text: Go Live of January 1, 2027 treated as firm for all modules. The City scores Implementation on Go Live for all modules by January 1, 2027, and the proposed solution commits to that date for Financials and HCM together. A full-scope ERP with data conversion, integrations, report development and training in roughly 22 months leaves little float, and any City-side delay in fit-gap, data cleansing or UAT sign-off pushes the date. Missing it risks the Implementation score, contractual damages and a hypercare period that runs unpaid. The date is both a scored criterion and, on the solution's reading, a contractual commitment covering every module; the RFP does not say whether it is binding or what happens if it slips, and the schedule depends on City resources the RFP does not quantify.
items.reason: Go Live for all modules by January 1, 2027 is scored and the implementation runs March 2025 to January 2027. Consequences need no support.

items.text: Page limit and proposal format ambiguities risk disqualification. The 100-page limit is stated twice with different wording, the required section order table is not in the RFP text, and the solution assumes the Word Requirements document sits outside the page count. If that reading is wrong, or if the response deviates from the prescribed format, the proposal can be classified non-responsive and disqualified before it is scored. The RFP says proposals deviating from the requested format may be disqualified, and the solution's page-count assumption is an inference from conflicting wording rather than a stated rule.
items.reason: The 100-page limit is stated twice, but the section order table is in S9.3, so 'not in the RFP text' is wrong.

items.text: Demo Script and demo logistics unavailable before finalist selection. Finalists must demo in December 2024 against a pre-defined Demo Script that is only issued with the finalist invitation, and the format, timing and location of the demos are not stated. The team cannot size demo preparation or guarantee the named presenters' availability, and a script that arrives late or covers unfamiliar scenarios weakens the Software and Implementation scores that carry 55 of the 100 points. The script is a referenced document not included in the RFP and the demo dates are fixed in the selection calendar, so preparation effort and staffing are committed against an unknown script.
items.reason: Demo script issued with finalist notification and December 2024 demos are supported. 'Format, timing and location not stated' is not shown; Software and Implementation weights of 30 and 25 are supported.

items.text: Insurance cover and limits unstated, so the premium cannot be priced. The RFP requires a certificate of insurance and an underwriter's endorsement with additional insured wording from a surety admitted in Washington, but states no coverage types, limits or additional insured parties. The bidder must either guess the cover in its price or leave it out and absorb the premium later, and an endorsement that does not match the City's wording can hold up the start of work. The solution prices insurance on an assumed set of coverages pending the City's limits, and the RFP gives none; the requirement is a condition of commencing work, so a mismatch delays mobilization.
items.reason: Certificate of insurance, underwriter's endorsement and Washington admitted surety are stated; no limits or coverage types appear.

items.text: Pricing held for 180 days across a selection calendar that runs past it. Pricing must remain valid for 180 days from the September 17, 2024 response, but negotiations begin in January 2025 and no contract is awarded until City Council approves it. A long negotiation, a Council deferral or a rescheduled selection can carry the bid past the validity window, forcing a re-price or an unpriced extension at the bidder's cost. The RFP reserves the right to modify or reschedule the selection schedule and requires Council approval before award, while the solution commits to a fixed 180-day hold with no escalation clause.
items.reason: The 180-day validity, September 17, 2024 due date, January 2025 negotiations, Council approval and right to reschedule are all stated.

items.text: Two deployment options priced on one effort estimate. The solution prices SaaS as the primary offer and on-premises as a separately sheeted alternative, but the RFP does not say which options must be priced or how the City will compare them. Preparing two full Exhibit A sheets doubles pricing effort and page count, and an on-premises option priced from SaaS assumptions may be materially understated if hardware, database licensing and patching obligations fall to the bidder. The RFP requires a separate sheet per deployment option without naming the options, and the solution's choice to price both is an inference that adds cost and risk to the bid itself.
items.reason: A separate pricing sheet per deployment option, with SaaS or on-premises options mentioned, is stated; the options are not named for pricing.

items.text: Configuration effort assumed included in the implementation price. The rating scale treats a 4 as available out of the box or with configuration included in the proposal, and the solution embeds configuration effort in the implementation services price rather than charging it separately. If the Requirements document contains many items that need configuration, the fixed implementation price absorbs work the bidder never separately estimated, and the City may read a 4 as a promise of no extra cost for any configuration it later requests. The RFP does not settle whether configuration is priced in the proposal or assumed free, and the solution resolves the ambiguity in the City's favour without a configuration volume estimate.
items.reason: Rating 4 definition includes configuration included in the proposal; implementation pricing includes system configuration; the RFP does not clarify further.

items.text: References may not satisfy undefined size and scope criteria. The RFP requires three current and two prior references similar in size and scope to the City's project, with preference for Washington public-sector clients, but does not define similar size, scope, or whether references must run the proposed modules. The solution assumes comparable Washington public-sector clients exist; if they do not, the Vendor criterion (15 points) is weakened and the bid may be judged less experienced than required. Neither the size threshold nor the module-match rule is stated, and the solution's reference set is an assumption rather than a confirmed list.
items.reason: Three current and two prior references, similar size and scope, Washington public-sector preference are stated; no size definition; Vendor criterion is 15 points.

items.text: Best-of-breed HCM integration obligation without a defined boundary. The RFP invites best-of-breed HCM responses provided the HCM solution integrates with the selected ERP, but does not say whether such a response must cover the full ERP scope or only HCM, or whether the City will contract with several vendors. The solution commits to full-scope ERP with best-of-breed integration demonstrated; if the City selects a separate HCM vendor, the integration work, its ownership and its cost fall between contracts. The RFP leaves the minimum scope of a best-of-breed response and the multi-vendor contracting model open, and the solution's full-scope assumption is an inference that may not match the City's intent.
items.reason: RFP invites best-of-breed HCM with ERP integration, requires full requirements and integrated ERP, and is silent on minimum scope and contracting model.

items.text: Unreadable page 5 may hide a submission or scope requirement. Page 5 of the RFP is largely an image that could not be parsed, and it sits in the early sections that carry the submission instructions and City background. A requirement, form or instruction on that page could be missed, and a missed submission instruction is a disqualification risk while a missed scope statement is a pricing risk. The page is 42% image and unreadable to the extraction, and the surrounding sections carry mandatory submission and scope content; the impact is high if it holds an instruction but the chance of a material omission is limited to one page.

Named bid team committed to selection events without a fee. The solution holds the engagement director, solution architect and module leads available for the December 2024 demo, January 2025 due diligence and negotiations from January 2025 without a separate fee, and the City reserves the right to reschedule. If the calendar moves or the process runs long, senior staff are tied up unpaid across several months while other work is turned away, and the bid cost rises with no guarantee of award. The RFP reserves the right to modify or reschedule the selection calendar, and the solution's commitment to named individuals across three windows is an assumption that the dates hold.
items.reason: Demo, due diligence, negotiation dates, rescheduling right and bidder bearing proposal costs are all in sources; staffing commitments are bidder positions.
